shots.say: What if sound... moved at walking speed?
Leo opened his book to a brand new chapter.
Sound is just air molecules bumping into each other, like falling dominoes. Normally, that chain races at 343 meters a second. Now slow it down... to a walking pace.
Talk to a friend across the room, and your words arrive two seconds late. Shout across a football field... they'd hear you over a minute later.
A storm two kilometers away? You'd see the lightning... and hear the thunder twenty-four minutes later.
Even a gentle breeze would outrun sound. Anyone upwind of you... couldn't hear you at all.
And anyone who jogs would break the sound barrier. Runners, bikes, cars... sonic booms all day long.
The wildest part? Scientists have really made sound this slow, in clouds of atoms colder than outer space. Could you survive a day in this world?
